newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Six killed in attack on Pakistan mosque.
newsitem.headline: Six killed in attack on Pakistan mosque.

text.p: Gunmen attacked a mosque in the Pakistani city of Lahore after evening prayers on Wednesday, killing at least six people, police said.
They said at least two other people were injured in the attack, which appeared to be the latest in a wave of Moslem sectarian violence in the populous Punjab province, of which Lahore is the capital.
Police said there were about five attackers but there was no immediate information about their identity. They fired from automatic weapons on the Sunni sect's Ziaul Uloom mosque in northern Lahore.

The attack was carried out hours after a young Shi'ite Moslem, Sahir Rizvi, was killed by unidentified gunmen in Lahore's busy Anarkali bazaar. Twelve people, most of them Shi'ites, were killed in three shootouts in Punjab on Monday.

Sectarian violence is rife in Punjab. Militant Sunni and Shi'ite factions are engaged in a feud that officials say has killed more than 100 people so far this year, including religious scholars, lawyers and doctors.

Sunni groups accuse neighbouring Shi'ite Iran of financing Pakistani Shi'ite militants, while Shi'ites accuse Sunni Saudi Arabia of aiding Sunni groups. Shi'ites form about 15 percent of Pakistan's mainly Sunni population of more than 135 million.
